Record Class InputContext

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.InputContext
Record Components:
originX - screen-space X of the element's containing content origin
originY - screen-space Y of the element's containing content origin
mouseX - screen-space mouse X of the event
mouseY - screen-space mouse Y of the event
disabled - whether the element's panel or container is disabled
public record InputContext(int originX, int originY, double mouseX, double mouseY, boolean disabled) extends Record
Input-time context passed to every PanelElement input method, the input twin of RenderContext (§0066): where the element's containing content origin is on screen, where the mouse is, and whether the element's surroundings are disabled.

Why input receives its context

Before 6.0.0, mouseClicked(mouseX, mouseY, button) had no origin, so an element that needed to know where it was (a Dropdown finding its popover, a ScrollContainer finding its scrollbar) cached the origin from its last render, and simple controls cached hovered from the last frame to gate their clicks. Each cache was a frame stale and each container re-derived its children's origins its own way. Now the dispatcher (the panel's host, or a container through ChildDispatch) hands every element the same facts render gets, for the moment of the event. No element caches its origin or its hover state.

Coordinates are screen space, as before: mouseX/mouseY are the event's position, originX/originY the content origin the element's childX/childY are relative to. A container passes its children at(int, int) their own origin.

Disabled

When disabled is true the dispatcher does not deliver clicks, wheel or keys at all (a disabled panel or container is inert inside, though it still claims its area). Releases and outside clicks still arrive with the flag set, so a drag or an open popover can end. An element also checks its own disabledWhen.
